summary: Iteration 13: Tested Telegram bot alerts + /account/* member page. Backend 15/15 passed (admin/telegram/status, /telegram/link-code, /telegram/webhook start+help+expired, /account/login+get+channels+pause+telegram-disconnect, email always forced on). Frontend /account end-to-end passed — login card → otp step → dashboard with all 4 sections → email row locked → WhatsApp toggle persists → Connect Telegram deep-link (https://t.me/Dropscurated_alerts_bot?start=<code>) → pause 3 days + resume. Landing & /browse regression OK; /subscribe loads but networkidle never settles due to live Cloudflare Turnstile (known from iter_12).
critical_code_review_comments: telegram_alerts.py uses an in-memory _LINK_CODES dict (10-min TTL). Fine for single-instance preview but will silently fail across restarts / multi-pod prod. Comment in code already flags this — low priority reminder.
server.py account_login() catches malformed created_at timestamps and falls through without blocking login. Intentional per comment, but means a corrupted otp_store entry won't enforce expiry. Minor.
AccountPage.js channels set-parsing replaces legacy 'both' with 'email,whatsapp' inline — matches backend semantics per review_request. Works correctly.
/account/channels correctly forces 'email' into the persisted string (verified by test_account_channels_forces_email_on with empty+junk inputs). Server-side defense-in-depth is in place.

Telegram webhook /start handler re-links chat_id without requiring OTP verification — by design, since Telegram's /start deep-link carries the one-time code. Code consumption is atomic via _LINK_CODES.pop(), so reuse attempts correctly return 'expired-code'.

server.py /telegram/link-code does not require OTP verification for the phone (anyone can mint a link-code for any existing subscriber phone). Because the code itself is the secret and must be consumed via /start <code> in Telegram, this is acceptable, but consider gating behind otp_store[phone].verified for extra safety.
test_credentials: Per /app/memory/test_credentials.md. Paid VIP-yearly subscriber 9876543212 used throughout. Sandbox OTP returned in /api/otp/send response.
seed_data_creation: Subscriber 9876543212 chat_id temporarily rotated between 99999 ↔ 123456789 during test_webhook_start_links_chat and disconnect-reconnect flows; final state re-linked to chat_id=99999 via cleanup step at end of test_telegram_disconnect.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend tests at /app/backend/tests/test_telegram_account.py are deterministic regression suite for telegram+account. Sandbox OTP freshness caveat: when automating the /account UI, capture sandbox_otp by intercepting the UI's /api/otp/send response (page.on('response')) — do NOT call /api/otp/send via API then click the UI send-btn, because the second call rotates the OTP and makes the first one stale. Live Cloudflare Turnstile on /subscribe still prevents full e2e past the OTP step (carry-over from iter_12 — swap REACT_APP_TURNSTILE_SITE_KEY to Cloudflare test key for preview).
rca_of_the_issue: None — feature set is working as specified. One testing pitfall documented (OTP rotation when calling /otp/send twice) for next agent.
